# RFC — Drop the `Luxen` prefix from public element classes

> Status: implemented in 0.5.0
> Branch: `refactor/rebrand-public-classes`

## Problem

luxen-ui ships as a white-label UI library. The intended consumer workflow is:

1. Pick a brand (e.g. `acme-ds`, `foo-design-system`).
2. Configure the Vite plugin with a custom prefix (`elementPrefix: 'acme'`, `cssPrefix: 'acme'`).
3. Build → custom elements register as `<acme-story>` instead of `<l-story>`, CSS selectors / tokens / keyframes rewrite to `acme-*` / `--acme-*`.
4. Re-export from the brand's package: `export { ... } from 'luxen-ui'`.

The runtime/CSS surface is fully prefix-agnostic thanks to `packages/ui/vite-plugin.ts` + `packages/ui/postcss-plugin-prefix.js`. **But the JavaScript class identifiers stay hardcoded as `LuxenStory`, `LuxenAvatar`, etc. — the brand leaks into the public TS API**, which contradicts the white-label principle.

A consumer building `acme-ds` ends up with `<acme-story>` in the DOM but `LuxenStory` in their TypeScript imports. They can alias on import (`import { LuxenStory as Story }`) but the friction is real and the brand inconsistency is on every API doc page.

### Inventory

22 public classes in `packages/ui/src/html/elements/*` (run `grep -rn "^export class " packages/ui/src/html/elements/` to refresh):

```
Avatar, Badge, Carousel, CarouselItem, Dialog, Divider, Drawer, Dropdown,
DropdownItem, Icon, InputOtp, InputStepper, Popover, Rating, Skeleton,
Spinner, Tabs, Toast, ToastItem, Tooltip, Tree, TreeItem
```

Plus the internal base classes `LuxenElement` and `LuxenFormAssociatedElement` in `packages/ui/src/html/shared/luxen-element.ts`, which keep their prefix.

## Resolution

**Dropped `Luxen` from the 22 public classes**: `LuxenAvatar` → `Avatar`, `LuxenStoriesViewer` → `StoriesViewer`, etc.

**Kept the internal base classes prefixed** (`LuxenElement`, `LuxenFormAssociatedElement`):

- `Element` collides with `globalThis.Element` (DOM interface). Hard collision, can't rename to plain `Element`.
- These are internal — not in the public package exports surface.

### Files affected

- 21× `packages/ui/src/html/elements/*/[name].ts` (the `toast` directory holds two classes in one file: `Toast` + `ToastItem`)
- 21× `packages/ui/src/html/elements/*/index.ts` — import + re-export + `HTMLElementTagNameMap` augmentation
- 3 cross-imports: `drawer/drawer.ts` (`Dialog`), `dropdown/dropdown.ts` (`DropdownItem`), `tree/tree.ts` (`TreeItem`)
- `AGENTS.md`, `packages/ui/CLAUDE.md`, `.agents/skills/luxen-design-principles/SKILL.md`, `.agents/skills/luxen-design-principles/references/typescript-patterns.md` — class names in examples
- `packages/ui/dist/custom-elements.json` (auto-regenerated by `cem analyze`)
- `packages/ui/dist/skills/luxen-ui/` (auto-regenerated by `scripts/generate-skill.mjs`)

### Build pipeline

The `vite-plugin.ts`, `postcss-plugin-prefix.js`, `scripts/generate-skill.mjs`, and CEM analyzer config all operate on **tag names** and **CSS prefixes**, not on JS class-name strings — no config change was required.

## Deferred sub-problem: `HTMLElementTagNameMap` augmentation

Default-prefix consumers keep IntelliSense (`'l-X': X` augmentations are still in place). Consumers who configure a custom `elementPrefix` (e.g. `acme-`) lose IntelliSense for the renamed tags — TypeScript module augmentation requires a static string literal and can't observe a runtime-configured prefix.

This pre-existing limitation is not aggravated by the rename. A separate RFC tracks the codegen helper that would emit a per-prefix augmentation file: see [`RFC-htmlelementtagnamemap-codegen.md`](./RFC-htmlelementtagnamemap-codegen.md).

## Out of scope

- Renaming the package itself (`luxen-ui` → something else) — separate concern.
- Renaming the internal `--l-*` token namespace — already handled by the postcss plugin at build time.
- Renaming the slash-imported subpath modules (`luxen-ui/story`, `luxen-ui/css/story`) — these are paths, not branding-sensitive in the same way.
- Renaming `LuxenElement` / `LuxenFormAssociatedElement` to `BaseElement` / `BaseFormAssociatedElement` — orthogonal cleanup, not picked up.
